name: LMDB
model: Library for sorted byte-string keys and values in named sub-databases, read through a memory map; cursors for range scans
engine_note: Copy-on-write B+tree in one memory-mapped file; no write-ahead log, no compaction; freed pages are reused
consistency: Full ACID transactions over many keys. Only one write transaction at a time, so writes are serializable; readers see a consistent snapshot and never block. Commit is fsynced by default (MDB_NOSYNC trades that away). One machine, no replication.
scaling: Single machine only; many reader threads and processes in parallel, one writer at a time. Size limited by disk and the address space of the map.
version_note: LMDB 1.0.0 was released 2026-06-30, the first 1.x after the long 0.9 line (0.9.36 last); the header tells 0.9 users to read upgrading notes.
reach: Reach for it when a read-heavy program needs a crash-safe local key-value store with very fast reads from many threads or processes (caches, indexes, metadata).
avoid: Avoid for write-heavy workloads with many concurrent writers, data shared across machines, or when you want SQL.
escape: You want crash-safe key-value storage inside your own process with near memory-speed reads.
chat: Nothing on the server side; possibly a local on-device cache in a desktop client.
notes: Surprise: LMDB reached 1.0 (1.0.0 on 2026-06-30, 1.0.1 on 2026-08-06) after more than a decade on 0.9.x; the header warns 0.9 users to read upgrading notes, so on-disk or API changes may apply (not checked in detail). Dates read from the CHANGES file in the LMDB_1.0.1 tag. No Jepsen report (embedded library).
